title: Stage 3: Multi-stage and cache-friendly
summary: Split build from runtime, and order the steps so a code edit rebuilds in seconds.

steps.title: Two fixes in one file
body: COPY TodoApi.csproj .                 # 1. only the project file...
RUN dotnet restore                    #    ...so this layer survives code edits
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS final     # 2. runtime only
rebuild after a       restore +      publish only

steps.prompt: Arrange the build stage so that `dotnet restore` stays cached when only `.cs` files change.
steps.explain: Project file, restore, then the rest of the source, then publish with `--no-restore`.

steps.prompt: You add a NuGet package (which edits `TodoApi.csproj`) and rebuild. What happens?
options: `COPY TodoApi.csproj .` misses, so restore and everything after it run again
The final stage is rebuilt but the build stage is cached
steps.explain: That is the right trade-off: restores happen only when dependencies change.

steps.prompt: A solution has `src/TodoApi/TodoApi.csproj` and `src/Domain/Domain.csproj` (referenced by the API). What must you copy before `dotnet restore`?
options: Both project files (and the .sln or Directory.Packages.props if used), at their relative paths
Nothing: restore downloads project references from NuGet
steps.explain: Restore follows project references, so every referenced .csproj must already be in place.

steps.title: Rewrite it as a cached multi-stage build
prompt: This terminal has a **real Docker Engine** with the **.NET 10 SDK and ASP.NET Core runtime images** loaded (no
network). `~/todo/Dockerfile` is the naive one-stage file. Rewrite it and build it as `todo:2`:
1. a `build` stage on `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0-alpine` that copies **only `TodoApi.csproj`** first, runs
`dotnet restore`, then copies the rest and runs `dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish --no-restore`;
2. a final stage on `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine` that copies only the publish output and starts
Run it as `todo` on port 8080 (`curl http://localhost:8080/health` prints `ok`), and compare
`docker image ls`: the new image should be a fraction of the naive one.

checks.name: todo runs from todo:2 and answers /health
checks.fail: There is no container `todo` from `todo:2` answering `http://localhost:8080/health`.

checks.name: the final image has the runtime but no SDK
checks.cmd: docker run --rm --entrypoint sh todo:2 -c 'test -x /usr/share/dotnet/dotnet && test ! -d /usr/share/dotnet/sdk && test ! -e /src && ls /app/TodoApi.dll'
checks.fail: `todo:2` should be the ASP.NET Core runtime image with only the publish output in `/app`: no SDK and no `/src`.

checks.name: it is a fraction of the SDK's size
checks.cmd: echo $(( $(docker image inspect -f '{{.Size}}' todo:2) / 1000000 )) MB | awk '{print ($1 < 250) ? "small" : $1 " MB is too big"}'
checks.fail: `todo:2` is still big: is the last stage `FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-alpine`?

checks.name: dotnet restore runs before the code is copied
checks.cmd: awk 'BEGIN{IGNORECASE=1} /^FROM/{stage++; csproj=0} /^COPY[^-]*\.csproj/{csproj=stage} /^RUN.*dotnet restore/{ if (csproj==stage) ok=stage } /^COPY[[:space:]]+\.[[:space:]]/{ if (ok==stage && ok>0) good=1; else if (!good) bad=1 } END{ print (good && !bad) ? "restore is cached" : "restore is not cached" }' ~/todo/Dockerfile
checks.fail: In the build stage, copy `TodoApi.csproj` and run `dotnet restore` **before** `COPY . .`, so a code change keeps the restore layer cached.

hints: Two `FROM`s: `... sdk:10.0-alpine AS build` and `... aspnet:10.0-alpine`; `COPY --from=build /app/publish .` moves the output.
Restore depends only on the project file: `COPY TodoApi.csproj .` then `RUN dotnet restore`, then `COPY . .`.
Then `docker build -t todo:2 ~/todo`, `docker rm -f todo` if it exists, and `docker run -d --name todo -p 8080:8080 todo:2`.
steps.explain: This is the Dockerfile shape Microsoft documents for .NET, and the one to recognise in any repository: SDK stage, restore layer keyed on the project files, publish, then the runtime image with only the output. For a solution with several projects, copy every `*.csproj` (and `Directory.Packages.props`, `NuGet.config`) before the restore. In CI, `RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.nuget/packages` makes even a changed restore fast.
